329890.title: The average-degree conjecture for minors of 2-regular graphs
329890.statement:
Let $H$ be a **$2$-regular graph** on $t$ vertices, and let $c$ be the number of odd-order connected components of $H$. Assume that $H$ is neither a $t$-vertex even cycle nor a disjoint union of $\tfrac{t}{4}$ cycles of order $4$.

**General 2-regular minor conjecture.** Every graph with average degree at least

$$
t+c-2
$$

and at least $t$ vertices contains $H$ as a minor.

This extends the Reed–Wood conjecture and the preceding odd- and even-parameter average-degree conjectures to an arbitrary prescribed $2$-regular graph. The supplied text gives no resolution and presents it as an open problem.

338234.title: Kanté–Kwon conjecture on vertex-minors of forests in graphs of large linear rank-width
338234.statement:
Let $T$ be a fixed forest, and let $f(T)$ denote an integer depending on $T$. A graph has **linear rank-width** at least $f(T)$ when its linear rank-width is at least that integer.

**Kanté–Kwon conjecture.** For every fixed forest $T$, there is an integer $f(T)$ such that every graph of linear rank-width at least $f(T)$ contains a vertex-minor isomorphic to $T$.

This conjecture is an analogue for linear rank-width of Oum's conjecture for rank-width. The source presents it as an open problem, and no resolution is given here.

340023.title: Fractional Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for subgraphs of prescribed girth
340023.statement: Let $x\ge1$ be real and let $g\ge3$ be an integer. For a graph $G$, let $\chi_f(G)$ denote its fractional chromatic number, and let the **girth** of a graph be the length of its shortest cycle. **Fractional Erdős–Hajnal conjecture.** For every real number $x\ge1$ and any integer $g\ge3$, there exists a positive number $k(x,g)$ such that every graph $G$ with $\chi_f(G)\ge k(x,g)$ contains a subgraph $H$ of girth at least $g$ and with $\chi_f(H)\ge x$. This extends the paper’s proved triangle-free case, corresponding to $g=4$, to arbitrary prescribed girth; the proposed general statement remains open.

340024.title: Erdős–Hajnal–Thomassen conjecture on high-chromatic subgraphs of prescribed girth and average degree
340024.statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $g\ge3$ be an integer. For a graph, its **chromatic number** is denoted by $\chi(G)$, its **average degree** is the average of its vertex degrees, and its **girth** is the length of its shortest cycle. **Erdős–Hajnal–Thomassen conjecture.** For every positive integers $k$ and $g\ge3$, there exists a positive number $c(k,g)$ such that every graph with chromatic number at least $c(k,g)$ contains a subgraph of girth at least $g$ and with average degree at least $k$. The source presents this as a weakening of the Erdős–Hajnal and Thomassen conjectures and gives no resolution; it remains open.

341359.title: Eventual sharpness conjecture for leaf-sensitive oriented-tree unavoidability
341359.statement: An **oriented tree** is an orientation of an undirected tree, a leaf is a vertex of degree one in its underlying tree, and a digraph is $m$-unavoidable if it is contained as a subdigraph in every tournament of order $m$. **Eventual sharpness conjecture.** For every fixed integer $k$, there is an integer $n_k$ such that every oriented tree of order $n\geq n_k$ with $k$ leaves is $(n+k-2)$-unavoidable. This holds for $k=2$ and $k=3$, by results cited in the source, while the assertion for general fixed $k$ is left as a conjecture.

341385.title: The De Bruijn–Erdős conjecture for finite connected graphs
341385.statement: Let $G$ be a finite connected graph with $n=|V(G)|$ and $n\geq 2$, equipped with its graph metric. For distinct vertices $u,v$, let the **line** $L_G(u,v)$ be the metric line determined by $u$ and $v$, and call a line **universal** if it contains every vertex of $G$. **Graph De Bruijn–Erdős conjecture.** Every finite connected graph with $n\geq 2$ has at least $n$ distinct lines, or has a universal line. This conjecture is the graph-metric special case of the metric-space conjecture and remains open.

342566.title: Kelly's conjecture on reconstructibility from vertex-deleted decks
342566.statement:
Let $l\in\mathbb{N}$. An $l$-card of a graph is an induced subgraph obtained by deleting $l$ vertices, and the corresponding deck is the multiset of all such cards. A graph is **$l$-reconstructible** if it is determined by this deck.

**Kelly's conjecture.** For $l\in\mathbb{N}$, there is an integer $M_l$ such that any graph with at least $M_l$ vertices is reconstructible from its deck of cards obtained by deleting $l$ vertices.

This is a more detailed version of the Reconstruction Conjecture. The original conjecture is the special case $M_1=3$; the asserted existence of a threshold for every $l$ remains open.

343364.title: The avoidable induced path conjecture
343364.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $P_k$ denote an induced path on $k$ vertices. An induced path $P$ is **avoidable** if every extension of $P$ is contained in an induced cycle, where an extension is an induced path obtained by adding one edge to $P$ at each end. **Avoidable induced path conjecture.** For every $k\ge 1$, every graph that contains an induced $P_k$ also contains an avoidable induced $P_k$. This conjecture would simultaneously generalize the avoidable-vertex theorem and the result that graphs with no induced cycles of lengths at least $k+3$ contain a simplicial induced $P_k$; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

343498.title: Planar equitable vertex arboricity conjecture
343498.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $va_{eq}^*(G)$ denote the least integer $k$ such that $G$ has an equitable tree-$k'$-coloring for every integer $k'\geq k$, where an equitable tree-$k'$-coloring has forest color classes whose sizes differ pairwise by at most $1$.

**Planar equitable vertex arboricity conjecture.** There exists a constant $k$ such that every planar graph is equitably tree-$k'$-colorable for every integer $k'\geq k$; equivalently,

$$
va_{eq}^*(G)\leq k.
$$

This conjecture was proposed by Wu, Zhang and Li and was later confirmed by Esperet, Lemoine and Maffray, who proved the stronger explicit bound $va_{eq}^*(G)\leq 4$ for every planar graph. Thus the conjecture is solved.

344219.title: List-coloring version of Linear Hadwiger's conjecture
344219.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let $K_t$ denote the complete graph on $t$ vertices. A graph is **$k$-list colorable** if every assignment of lists of at least $k$ colors to its vertices admits a proper coloring from those lists. **List-coloring version of Linear Hadwiger's conjecture.** There exists $C>0$ such that for every integer $t\geq 1$, every graph with no $K_t$ minor is $Ct$-list colorable. This strengthens the ordinary linear coloring conjecture because list colorability implies ordinary colorability. Results showing that some graphs excluding complete minors require more than the corresponding constant list size leave the conjectured linear bound open.

344401.title: Gir3o et al.'s generalized majority coloring conjecture
344401.statement: For $3b1\in[0,1]$, an $3b1$-majority coloring of a digraph is a vertex-coloring in which, for every vertex $v$, at most $3b1\cdot d^+(v)$ out-neighbors have the same color as $v$. A digraph is $3b1$-majority $\ell$-choosable if such a coloring exists for every assignment of lists of size at least $\ell$ to its vertices. **Gir3o et al.'s conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq1$, every digraph $D$ has a $\frac{1}{k}$-majority $(2k-1)$-coloring; in fact, every digraph is $\frac{1}{k}$-majority $(2k-1)$-choosable. The known bound is $\frac{1}{k}$-majority $2k$-choosability for every integer $k\geq1$, so the conjecture asks whether one fewer color always suffices, even in the list-coloring setting.

346147.title: Kelly's $[?]$-reconstruction conjecture
346147.statement: For a graph $G$, write $\mathcal{D}_{|V(G)|-\ell}(G)$ for the multiset of induced subgraphs obtained by deleting $\ell$ vertices, and call $G$ **$\ell$-reconstructible** if this deck determines $G$ up to isomorphism. **Kelly's $\ell$-reconstruction conjecture.** For every $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$, there is an integer $M_\ell$ such that every graph with at least $M_\ell$ vertices is $\ell$-reconstructible. This generalizes Ulam's conjecture from deletion of one vertex to deletion of any fixed number of vertices; it remains open in general, though many graph properties and restricted graph classes are known to satisfy analogous bounds.

346570.title: Exponential flow-count conjecture for 3-edge-connected graphs
346570.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a 3-edge-connected oriented graph of order $n$, let $\text{?}$ be an abelian group with $|\text{?}| \text{?} 6$, and let $f:E\to\text{?}$. A flow $\text{?}:E\to\text{?}$ avoids $f$ if $\text{?}(e)\ne f(e)$ for every $e\in E$.

**Exponential flow-count conjecture.** There exists a fixed constant $c>1$ such that, for every such $G$, $\text{?}$, and $f$, there are at least $c^n$ flows $\text{?}$ avoiding $f$.

The paper presents this as a conjectural strengthening of its counting theorem, which gives exponential many avoiding flows for group orders at least $8$ but only existence for orders $6$ and $7$. Its status is not resolved in the supplied material.

347138.title: Rooted non-separating out-branching conjecture
347138.statement: Let $D$ be a digraph on at least $L$ vertices. Write $\lambda(D)$ for its arc-connectivity and $\alpha(D)$ for its independence number, and let $B_s^+$ denote an out-branching rooted at $s$. A **non-separating out-branching** is an out-branching with the non-separation property studied in the paper. **Rooted non-separating out-branching conjecture.** There exists an integer $L$ such that every digraph $D$ on at least $L$ vertices with $\lambda(D)\geq 2$ and $\alpha(D)=2$ has a non-separating out-branching $B_s^+$ for every choice of $s\in V$. The source notes that an infinite class of examples has such a branching from every vertex, but does not resolve the conjecture.

347274.title: Mondrian partition existence conjecture for squares
347274.statement:
Let $S$ be a square, and let $k$ be the number of rectangles in a partition. A **proper perfect Mondrian partition** is the paper's specified partition of $S$ into $k$ pairwise non-congruent rectangles of equal area. **Mondrian partition existence conjecture.** Given a square $S$, there is a proper perfect Mondrian partition

$$
\mathcal{P}=\{R_1,\dots,R_k\}
$$

of $S$ if and only if $k\geq 7$. The paper gives examples and constructions for several values of $k$ and conjectures that the stated threshold is exact for all positive integers $k$.

348099.title: Uniform entropy lower bound conjecture for proper subgraphs of metric graphs
348099.statement: Let $r\geq 3$. A metric graph of rank $r$ has **unit entropy** when its entropy is normalized to equal $1$, and a subgraph is **proper** when it is a strict subgraph of the graph. **Uniform entropy lower bound conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>0$ such that every metric graph of rank $r$ with unit entropy contains a proper subgraph with entropy at least $C$. This conjecture would provide a uniform way to move from arbitrary points in the entropy metric space toward completion points represented by unit-entropy metrics on proper subgraphs, supporting an inductive approach to the boundedness question for $(\mathcal{X}^1(\mathbb{F}_r),d_\mathfrak{h})$.

354329.title: Erdős's high-girth Steiner system conjecture
354329.statement: Given $n\ge q>r\ge2$, an **$(n,q,r)$-Steiner system** is a collection of $q$-element subsets of an $n$-element set in which every $r$-element subset lies in exactly one block. A **$(j,i)$-configuration** is a set of $i$ blocks spanning at most $j$ vertices. **Erdős's conjecture.** For every integer $g\ge2$, there exists $n_g$ such that for all admissible $n\ge n_g$, there exists an $(n,3,2)$-Steiner system with no $(i+2,i)$-configuration for all $2\le i\le g$. This was fully proved by Kwan, Sah, Sawhney, and Simkin, while earlier work established approximate versions.

355847.title: The triangle lower-bound conjecture for intersecting pseudocircle arrangements
355847.statement:
Let ${\cal A}$ be a simple arrangement of $n\ge 3$ pairwise intersecting pseudocircles, and let $p_3({\cal A})$ denote the number of triangular cells. **Triangle lower-bound conjecture.** Every such arrangement contains at least $n-1$ triangles:

$$
p_3({\cal A})\ge n-1.
$$

The bound is known to be tight for $3\le n\le 7$ by computer-assisted exhaustive enumeration, while the paper leaves open whether it is a tight lower bound for every $n\ge 3$.

381276.title: Stability conjecture for contact numbers of nearly congruent disks
381276.statement:
Let $n\ge 2$ and consider a packing of $n$ circular disks whose radii all lie in an interval $[1-\epsilon,1]$. **Stability conjecture.** There exists an $\epsilon>0$ such that, for every such packing, the number of touching pairs is at most

$$
\left\lfloor 3n-\sqrt{12n-3}\right\rfloor.
$$

This conjecture asks whether Harborth's exact contact-number bound for congruent disks remains valid for disks whose radii are sufficiently close to one. The source describes this stability version as an open problem; it is relevant to the optimization of colloidal clusters, where maximizing contacts favors low potential energy.

382235.title: Polynomial-time conjecture for Hamiltonian cycles after adding fixed vertices
382235.statement:
A **semicomplete digraph** is a digraph in which every pair of distinct vertices is joined by at least one directed arc. Fix an integer $k$. Consider digraphs obtained from a semicomplete digraph by adding $k$ new vertices and an arbitrary set of arcs involving the new vertices.

**Conjecture on fixed-vertex extensions.** For every fixed integer $k$, there exists a polynomial-time algorithm for deciding whether such a digraph has a Hamiltonian cycle.

The source states that this conjecture is open already for $k=2$. The resulting digraph need not be a split digraph because arcs may be added between the new vertices.
